rows.abstract: Rationale: "Security guards complement the policemen. In protecting the peace and securing life and property. To discharge their functions, security guards are usually issued serrvice firearms.  As such therefore, proper safeguards must be in placeto prevent abuse. Crimes committed by security guards using their service firearms have in fact been reported." Presccribes penalty for violation of this Act.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR NON-COMPLIANCE WITH STANDARD REQUIREMENTS OF FIRE SAFETY, CLEANLINESS AND HEALTH CONDITIONS IN DORMITORIES AND BOARDING HOUSES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Provides for the following --- "SECTION 1. Facilities for Fire Safety, Cleanliness and Health Conditions in Dormitories and Boarding Houses. - Dormitories and boarding houses shall have facilities and equipments for fire safetysanitatio n, cleanliness and health in accordance th the standards to be set by the Housing and Land Use Regulatory board (HLURB)." "SECTION 2. Penalties for Violations. - The owner and/or landlord of dormitories and boarding houses who fails to provide the facilities hereinabove required in compliance with the set standards shall, without prejudice to the penalties provided by other laws, be punished by a fine of not less than ten thousand pesos (P10,000.00) and/or imprisonment of not more than one year."
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SECURITY since 1996-07-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT ALLOWING POWER CONSUMERS TO REVOKE THE FRANCHISE OF POWER PRODUCERS AND DISTRIBUTORS THROUGH REFERENDUM
rows.abstract: Seeks to provide a mechanism by which power producers and distributors may be compelled to be reliable and efficient by the threat of revocation of their exclusive franchises through referendum among power consumers. Such a referendum may be held atregular intervals covering a reasonable period of time.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on  since 1996-07-24

rows.abstract: States that --- "SECTION 1. Prohibition. - Any agency of government or private entities deputized by government to collect garbage is hereby prohibited from dumping collected garbage in any site within one kilometer radius of a residential area." penalizes violation of this Act.

rows.abstract: Provides for the following --- "THE VOLUNTARY ARBITRATOR OR PANEL OF VOLUNTARY ARBITRATORS SHALL HAVE THE POWER TO REQUIRE ANY PERSON TO ATTEND HEARING/S AS A WITNESS.  THEY SHALL HAVE THE POWER TO SUBPOENA WITNESSES AND DOCUMENTS WHEN THE RELEVANCYOF THE TESTIMONY AND THE MATERIALITY THEREOF HAVE BEEN DEMONSTRATED TO THE ARBITRATORS. IN THE EXERCISE OF HIS POWERS UNDERR THIS CODE, THE VOLUNTARY ARBITRATOR OR PANEL OF VOLUNTARY ARBITRATORS MAY HOLD ANY PERSON IN DIRECT OR INDIRECT CONTEMPT ANDIMPOSE THE APPROPRIATE PENALTIES THEREOF."

rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING EMPLOYERS TO FURNISH EMPLOYEES COPIES OF THE EMPLOYMENT CONTRACTS AND TO MAKE A SWORN DECLARATION THEREFOR, AMENDING FOR THIS PURPOSE ARTICLE 279 OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 442, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LABOR CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES

rows.abstract: "SECTION 1. Notwithstanding any law to the contrary, public and private buildings for public use, educational institutions, airports, sports and recreation centers and complexes, shopping centers or establishments, workplaces, public utilities shallreserve sufficient and suitable parking or seating spaces for the use of expectant mothers." "SECTION 2. In case of public transportation , devices such as the prominent display of posters or stickers shall be used to generate public awareness of the rights herein instituted and foster understanding of the special circumstances of expectant mothers. Discrimination against expectant mothers in the carriage or transportation of passengers is hereby declared unlawful.

rows.title_full: AN ACT TRANSFERRING TO THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS THE MANAGEMENT ADMINISTRATION AND OPERATION OF MUNICIPAL PORTS TO THE LOCAL GOVENMENT UNITS WITHIN WHOSE TERRITORIAL JURISDICTION THE SAME ARE SITUATED REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NUMBERED FIVE HUNDRED AND FIVE, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: Rationale: "Recent developments however point that there is a growing clamor from the local government officials that greater efficiency and productivity could be achieved if the management and operations of these ports be transferred to them.  A factor for consdieration is the fact that each port and its immediate envisions offer possibilities for development if taken into consideration along that with the development thrusts of the province or municipality. In effect, the idea is that, sincethe local officials are in the best position to char the development areas and that maritime transportation is a vital cog in these efforts, they will be in a better capacity to handle the managementm, supervision and operations of these ports."
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION AND COMMUNICATIONS since 1996-07-25

rows.abstract: Mandates the proposed Office to: (a) promote efficiency and effectiveness in the delivery of basic services to the people. (b) Maintain as integrated human resource system characterized by independence, objectivity and integrity in order to enhanceresponsiveness to the requirements of an effective bureaucracy. (c) Promote and develop a reliable data system and personnel movement that will give support to the needs of the an efficient civil service and an accurate guide to the Department of Budget and Management, so that the decision making process will be made relative easier. >Prescribes the powers and functions of the Office.

rows.abstract: Provides for the following --- "SECTION 1. This act shall provide for the adjustment of Social Security System monthly pension to three thousand pesos (P3,000.00), provided that in the succeeding years upon approval of this Act, said amount will beincreased annually by not less than One thousand five-hundred pesos P1,500.00) until the total monthly pension shall be at least Six thousand pesos (P6,000.00) per month."
rows.status: Substituted by HB07758

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 33 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991, EXEMPTING COOPERATIVE VENTURES FROM TAXES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Amends Section 33 of RA 7160 to read as follows: "SECTION 33. COOPERATIVE UNDERTAKINGS AMONG LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS. - Local government units may, through appropriate ordinances, group themselves, consolidate, CREATE SUBSIDIARY CORPORATIONS, COOPERATIVE VENTURES or coordinate their efforts, services and resources for purposes commonly beneficial to them.  In support of such undertakings, the local government units involved may, upon approval by the sanggunian concerned after a public hearing conducted for the purpose, contribute funds, real estate, equipment, and other kinds of property and appoint or assign personnel under such terms and conditions as may be agreed upon by the participating local units through Memoranda of Agreement. SUCHH UNDERTAKINGS SHALL BE IN THE NATURE OF COOPERATIVE JOINT VENTURES AND SHALL BE EXEMPT FROM TAXES IN ACCORDANCE WITH EXISTING POLICES."
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 1996-07-25

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 3 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160 OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991, PROVIDING FOR SELECTIVE DECENTRALIZATIO N OF CERTAIN FUNCTIONS TO LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: "Devolution has hastened country-wide modernization which had long been hampered by a highly centralized system of government. It has provided for a more responsive and accountable local government structure instituted through a system ofdecentralizatio n whereby LGUs are given more power, authority, responsibilitie s and resources.  > However, the Local Government Code is not flexible enough to anticipate succeeding functions that may well be subject of decentralizatio n." Amends Section 3. of RA 7160 to read ad follows: "SECTION 3. OPERATIVE PRINCIPLES OF DECENTRALIZATIO N - The formulation and implementation of policies and measures on local autonomy shall be guided by the following operative principles: (a) There shall be aan effective allocation among the different local government units of their respective powers, functions, responsibilitie s, and resources; (b) THE NATIONAL GOVERNMENT THROUGH THE PRESIDENT MAY DECENTRALIZE OTHER POWERS AND AUTHORITIES CURRENTLY VEST
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 1996-07-25

rows.author: A074
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING ALL FRANCHISE HOLDERS OR OPERATORS OF TELEVISION STATIONS, PRODUCERS OF TELEVISION PROGRAMS, HOME VIDEO PROGRAMS AND MOTION PICTURES TO HAVE THEIR PROGRAMS AND FILMS BROADCAST WITH CLOSED-CAPTION AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF
rows.abstract: Defines "CLOSED-CAPTION " as a method of captioning or subtitling of television home video programs and films for hearing-impaire d or foreign language viewers without interfering with the normal television pciture and films, by coding captions as vertical interval data signal which is decoded at the receiver and superimposed on the television picture or on films of motion pictures. Penalizes violation of this Act.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC INFORMATION since 1996-07-25

rows.author: A013
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO PROMOTE PRODUCTIVE USE OF IDLE PUBLIC AND PRIVATE AGRICULTURAL LANDS THROUGH BUILD-OPERATE-T RANSFER SCHEMES IN FAVOR OF FARMWORKERS
rows.abstract: Declares it the policy og the State to --- (a) Encourage private investments and renewed corporation or cooperative activities in idle public and private agricultural lands through "Build-Operate- Transfer Schemes" in favor of farmworkers. (b)  Promote the development of idle public and private agricultural lands and make them economically productive and sustainable; and (c) Enahnce productivity and income of farmer/farmwork ers and the rural population. Covers all idle public and private agricultural lands and allow any productive enterprise engaged in: agricultural production, agri-processing or manufacturing, agri-trading, agro-tourism, etc.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRARIAN REFORM since 1996-07-25

rows.author: A013
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROMOTING A SMALL BUSINESS INCUBATOR PROGRAM
rows.abstract: Defines "BUSINESS INCUBATOR" as an organization set up for the specific purpose of nurturing young enterprises by providing common office and service facilities; a wide-range of services, and technical advice and information at below-market costs. Identifies the services provided by such business incubators,a s well as the types of incubators be established; sets the general guidelines for setting up said incubator.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ECONOMIC AFFAIRS since 1996-07-25

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE ESTABLISHMENT OF LABOR-MANAGEMEN T COOPERATIVES IN BUSINESS FIRMS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Rank and file workers employed by private business firms compose a major segment of the entire Filipino population. While they are more fortunate than many of our brethren who have no jobs, yet in many instances their monthly income cannot support their present and future needs, much less if they have families. Seeks to compel workers to save, as well as to oblige management in providing said capital in the establishment of a Labor Management Cooperative within the covered business firm.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 1996-07-25

rows.author: A013
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING TAX INCENTIVES TO PRIVATE AND GOVERNMENT-OWNE D AND -CONTROLLED CORPORATIONS FOR THE PROMOTION OF EMPLOYEES STOCK OWNERSHIP PLAN
rows.abstract: Defines ESOP-EMPLOYEE STOCK OWNERSHIP as a contribution plan in which the sponsoring employer or corporation makes regular contributions which accumulate to produce a benefit for employees,  In return, ESOP sponsors shall receive various tax incentives as provided in this Act. Technically, it is a stock bonus plan for the employees designed to invest primarily in the sponsoring employer's stocks or securities. It rewards employees with a benefit tied to corporate performance. Provides for: (1)Methods of Contributions; (2) Limits to Contributions; (3) Entitlement to Fair Market Value; (4) Tax Incentives.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 1996-07-25

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION TWENTY FIVE LETTER B OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991, REQUIRING ALL NATIONAL PROGRAMS AND PROJECTS WHICH ARE LOCATION SPECIFIC TO BE INTEGRATED WITH LOCAL DEVELOPMENT PLANS, ANDFOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: To enhance intergovernment al relations between national agencies and the local government units.  With the President exercising genreal sueprvision over the local government units, the national agencies and offices which are tasked withimplementing programs in the local level are likewise given the mandate to ensure that the LGU's are encouraged to participate in these development undertakings. Mandates all national agencies to submit all national programs, projects and plans whichare location specific to a province, city or municipality to the local government unit concerned for integration with the Local Development Plan.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 1996-07-25

rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING A PUBLIC MARKET DEVELOPMENT FUND AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Rationale: A development fund to oversee the standardization of public market facilities. One need not overemphasize the necessity of providing for a uniform standard available for each public market, laying emphasis on environmental concerns, sanitation and upgrading support facilities because majority of the population primarily go to public markets for their daily food requirements and other commodities. > A council on the national level with a direct, and consulative linkage with the localmarket officials through a regional committee which shall in joint and collaborative efforts issue the necessary rules and regulations for the effective implementation of this Act and maintain a continuind coordination to ensire that the objectives oof this law are eventually met.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 1996-07-25

rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING THE COMPLETE PRIVATIZATION OVER THREE YEARS OF REMAINING GOVERNMENT ENTERPRISES PROVIDING NON-ESSENTIAL SERVICES OR COMPETING WITH PRIVATE ENTERPRISES
rows.abstract: Seeks to restore the momentum of putting the private sector in the lead of government's effort to attain development. Requires, therefore, that the ramaining government enterprises providing non-essential services or competing with private enterprises shall, over a period of THREE (3) YEARS, be sold to the private sector.

rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTING A PROFIT-SHARING- SCHEME BASED ON EMPLOYEE PRODUCTIVITY
rows.abstract: Seeks to make PROFIT-SHARING a major feature in labor-managemen t relations in the country. Provides that FIFTY PERCENT (50%) of the NET INCOME of private enterprises EXCEEDING TWO HUNDRED PERCENT (200%) of the AVERAGE RETURN ON INVESTMENT from treasury bills issued shall be shared with all employees based on their performance.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 1996-07-29

rows.abstract: Amends Sections 5 & 7 of Chapter 11 of R.A. 6657 in order to ensure continuing distribution of lands to landless farmers over a period of TWENTY (20) YEARS. Intends to afford the government ample time to implement and fully realize the objective ofthe CAR Law.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A NATIONAL BAMBOO AND RATTAN DEVELOPMENT PROGRAM HARMONIZING ECOLOGICAL BALANCE WITH INDUSTRIAL DEVELOPMENT AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Rationale: Government suspport for the intensive development of bamboo and rattan farms owned by forest dwellers and the rural poor can be a strategic move in upgrading the quality of life of Filipino which obviously should start from the grassroots. Proposes a bamboo and rattan development program covering the following phases: (1) propagation or production of high quality, genetically superior planting stocks through sexual and macro and micro-asexual means; (2) dispersal or distribution of planting materials to be disposed at nominal amounts; (3) production or bamboo farming and/or plantation development and management; (4) utilization, processing and marketing including high value product development; (5) training and extension, includding technology packaging and transfer; and (6) research and technology.

rows.abstract: "Professionals Volunteer Act of 1996" Rationale: A 1993 survey shows that there are only 6,913 government doctors and 1,895 government dentists to attend to a population of 68 million Filipinos. > As it is also the State's policy to inculcate socialresponsibility, this bill seeks tap professionals who have been granted the privilege to practice their professions to render volunteer work as a requisite for the renewal of their license.

rows.abstract: "Government Office Library Act of 1996" States that --- "SECTION 4. Establishment of Libraries - All government agencies, including their regional and provincial offices shall establish a library where the following data shall be filed for access tothe public: (1) publications and newsletters of the agency, (2) all the latest data or statistics, including raw and uncollated data, which the agency has gathered or used as a basis for its operations; (3)  official repoorts and office memoranda that concern the public, such as progress reports on its projects, situationers and the like, (4) administrative issuances, implementing guidelines and regulatory orders issued by the agency and laws and other executives issuances tht cocnern the agenccy, (5) and annual reports.

rows.title_full: AN ACT ALLOWING TUITION FEES PAID FOR THE EDUCATION OF CHILDREN DEDUCTIBLE FROM GROSS INCOME OF INDIVIDUAL TAXPAYERS
rows.abstract: Proposes to add this NEW paragraph to SEction 29, National Internal Revenue Code to read as follows: "(N) DEDUCTION ALLOWABLE FROM THE GROSS INCOME OF FILIPINO INDIVIDUAL TAXPAYERS. - IN COMPUTING THE TAXABLE INCOME OF A FILIPINO INDIVIDUAL TAXPAYER, REGARDLESS OF WHETHER OR NOT HE IS A COMPENSATION INCOME EARNER, ENGAGED IN BUSINESS OR TRADE, OR IN PRACTICE OF PROFESSION, THERE SHALL BE ALLOWED A DEDUCTION IN HIS GROSS INCOME FIFTY (50%) OF THE TOTAL AMOUNT PAID FOR MATRICULATION FEES FOR THEEDUCATION OF HIS CHILDREN IN ANY GIVEN YEAR WHICH SHALL IN NO CASE EXCEED THE AMOUNT OF TWENTY PESOS (P20,000.00) SUBJECT, HOWEVER, TO THE FOLLOWING CONDTIONS."
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 1996-07-30
